name: Curator
description: Asks an LLM what your library has in common and builds the answers into ordered playlists surfaced as home screen rows.
overview: LLM-inferred vibe categories for your Jellyfin library.

versions.changelog: The weather and time-of-day rows become ONE row for the moment you are in, titled for the pair — "Rainy Night Cozy Vibes", "Cloudy Morning Stories". Two strict rows were empty exactly when most wanted: on a 202-item library "cloudy and morning" described one film and "rain and morning" described none. The single row grades instead of filtering, so something suiting both the sky and the hour leads, then the weather, then the hour — and it still draws when the weather cannot be read. One row per viewer when each has their own location. Also from 0.8.2.0: the settings tabs stretch to the full page width like Schedule, Runs and Usage; the condensed summaries list is scrollable with a pinned header, sorts A to Z, shows Weather and When columns, and no longer touches its frame; and Save sits at the top of each tab.

Full coverage of every weather code Open-Meteo reports, with stand-ins so a thunderstorm row falls back to rain-suited titles rather than showing nothing. Optionally reads tone descriptions from the Concierge search plugin as extra input when condensing.
Shows the running plugin version on the configuration page, so a browser-cached page is obvious at a glance. The weather test now logs its result server-side as well as showing it.
Fixes the weather test button reporting failure for lookups that had actually succeeded, and makes it report the real reason when one genuinely fails.
